Business domain map: Bunkai

What Bunkai is for, how it earns, and what every domain term means. Built from the app repo ../upex-bunkai-tms (branch staging, 67 migrations) and the legacy markdown under .context/business/, which was written against 12 migrations and is now partly stale.

Overview

Confidence: High. The schema (67 migrations, each with a header that states its intent) is the primary signal; the app README.md is the generic boilerplate README and carries no product signal.

Problem statement

Bunkai (分解, "decomposition") is a Test Management System (TMS) for QA teams. It addresses the traceability gap between business intent and tests: every Acceptance Test Case (ATC) must reference at least one Acceptance Criterion of a user story, so no test exists without a business reason (supabase/migrations/0004_atcs.sql, the "anchoring moat"). DESIGN.md frames it as a developer-first, dense, keyboard-driven tool for people who handle hundreds of ATCs a day.

The product has grown past authoring. It now chains ATCs into reusable Tests (0024_tests.sql), executes them as Runs against a project environment with a frozen snapshot of every step (0031_runs.sql), files Bugs from failed steps (0046_bugs.sql), tracks Milestones (0064_milestones.sql), imports user stories from Jira (0019_import_jobs.sql) and notifies people about run and bug events (0053_notifications.sql).

Target users

  • QA engineers who author ATCs and execute Runs (workspace role member).
  • QA leads who manage the team and its access (roles admin, owner).
  • Read-only stakeholders such as developers or product people (role viewer).
  • Automation: CI pipelines and AI agents using Personal Access Tokens; a Run records whether it was executed by a human, an agent or ci (runs.executor_mode).

Value proposition

Traceable acceptance testing in one multi-tenant tool: stories and criteria, the ATCs anchored to them, Tests that chain ATCs, Runs with immutable evidence, and Bugs linked back to the step that failed. Delivered today in the code; the paid plans are declared but not enforced (see Business model).

QA relevance

Business aspectTesting implication
Multi-tenancy with row-level securityCross-workspace isolation is the top risk: a user must never read or write another workspace's data, and a foreign environment answers 404 (0063_environment_cross_workspace_404.sql)
Roles viewer / member / admin / ownerEvery write path needs an allowed and a denied case per role
Anchoring moatSaving an ATC with no acceptance criterion must fail
Run snapshotsEditing an ATC after a Run started must not change that Run's steps
Bug provenanceA Bug filed from a failed run step keeps its run, step and ATC links; a standalone Bug has none
Token scopesEach scope tested as permitted and as denied
Magic-link loginBrowser tests cannot read the email; headless tests authenticate another way (see infra-context)

Acceptance criterion

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Acceptance criterionAcceptanceCriterion"Manage criteria"acceptance_criteria0003_authoring.sql, 0017

Acceptance Test Case (ATC)

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Acceptance Test CaseAtc"ATC Library", "New ATC"atcs0004_atcs.sql, lib/types.ts, nav label

Business meaning: the atomic, reusable test of one behaviour, with ordered steps and assertions, a test layer (UI, API, Unit) and tags. Lives in the project's ATC Library, can be searched, duplicated and reused by many Tests; an edit propagates to every Test that chains it (0035).

Abbreviations: ATC. Related terms: ATC step, ATC assertion, Test.

Not the same as a Jira Test issue: in this repo's QA process an ATC is also the KATA name for an automated test component.

Run

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Test run (execution)runs"Test Runs"runs0031_runs.sql, nav label

Business meaning: one execution of a Test against a project environment, by a human, an agent or CI. Starting it freezes a snapshot of every chain position and step, so later ATC edits never rewrite past evidence. A Run can be finished or aborted and keeps a history.

Related terms: Run ATC, Run step, Project environment, Bug.

Bug

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTableFound in
Bug (Jira prose: "defect")bugs"Bug Reports"bugs0046_bugs.sql, nav label

Business meaning: a product defect filed inside Bunkai, either from a failed run step (it then keeps the run, step and ATC as provenance) or standalone. Always belongs to a project and a module, has a severity from P1 to P4, a status and an assignee.

Naming: the migration says "bug" is the domain-glossary term while Jira prose keeps saying "defect". This repo's QA process also distinguishes Bug from Defect by lifecycle stage; inside Bunkai's data model there is only bugs.

Discovery gaps

  • Revenue model: workspace plans are declared but no payment provider or plan gating exists. Business rules per plan need product input.
  • Term structure: attributes, relationships and state machines of every term belong to business-data-context, which is still a placeholder (project-context mode data). Each term's "Structure" pointer is pending until then.
  • UI labels marked "not verified": no i18n bundle exists, so labels come from hardcoded component text; labels for members, steps, assertions, chain positions, run snapshots, environments, invites, import jobs and preferences were not found.
  • Bug vs defect: the UI says "Bug Reports", the table is bugs, Jira prose says "defect". Confirm which name ATPs and test names should use.
  • Milestone lifecycle: no status column found on milestones; whether a milestone can be completed or archived is unknown.
  • Reports (project coverage, recovery cycle, defect heatmap) are business concepts without their own table; they belong to the data and E2E maps.
  • No figures: the diagrams capability (diagram-design skill) is not installed; this map is tables only, which the glossary allows.
